title: Perfectness with tor amplitude in a range can be checked on residue fields at maximal ideals
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, integers a and b, and a pseudo-coherent complex K^bullet of R-modules, and proves the equivalence of three conditions: K^bullet is perfect with tor amplitude in [a, b]; for every prime p the cohomology H^i(K^bullet tensor^L_R kappa(p)) vanishes for i outside [a, b]; and the same vanishing for every maximal ideal m (source lines 20031-20045). The proof omits the implications (1) => (2) => (3) (proof line 20048), so the substantive content is (3) => (1). Assuming (3), fix i outside [a, b]; the cut-complex statement shows the assumption implies H^i(K^bullet)_m = 0 for all maximal ideals, hence H^i(K^bullet) = 0 (proof lines 20049-20053). The cut-complex statement is then used again to show that for every maximal ideal m there is an element f not in m such that K^bullet tensor_R R_f is perfect with tor amplitude in [a, b] (proof lines 20054-20059). The conclusion follows from the two gluing statements for perfectness and for tor amplitude (proof lines 20059-20060). The non-routine content is the two-step use of the cut-complex statement: first to kill the individual cohomology modules locally, then to produce a localizing element on which the amplitude condition holds.
